scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Eco-certification of Coffee
description:
The Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Eco-certification of Coffee scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2017. 

This initiative aims to enhance the quality of coffee produced in traditional coffee-growing regions. 

The scheme is specifically designed to promote sustainable practices among coffee farmers. 

The primary objective is to facilitate eco-certification for coffee produced in these areas. 

The government aims to increase the income of coffee growers by ensuring that their products meet international standards. 

By 2022, the target was to have at least 50% of coffee produced in traditional areas certified under eco-friendly standards. 

The scheme also aims to improve the marketability of Indian coffee on a global scale. 

It seeks to enhance the competitiveness of Indian coffee in international markets. 

The benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for farmers to adopt eco-friendly practices. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 50,000 per hectare for implementing sustainable agricultural practices. 

The scheme also provides training and capacity-building programs for farmers. 

These programs focus on organic farming techniques and sustainable coffee cultivation methods. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a registered coffee grower in traditional coffee-growing areas. 

Farmers must also have a minimum of 1 hectare of land under coffee cultivation. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 3 lakh per annum for individual farmers. 

Cooperatives and groups of farmers can also apply for the scheme. 

They must have a minimum of 10 members and be registered under relevant cooperative laws. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, farmers must fill out the application form available at the local coffee board office. 

They need to submit proof of land ownership and registration as a coffee grower. 

Farmers must also provide income proof to demonstrate eligibility. 

After submission, the application is reviewed by the local coffee board officials. 

Once approved, farmers receive a confirmation and are guided on the next steps. 

The disbursement of funds occurs in two phases. 

The first phase involves an initial payment of 50% of the total assistance amount. 

This is provided after the approval of the application. 

The remaining 50% is disbursed after the successful implementation of eco-certification practices. 

The timeline for the entire process from application to fund disbursement can take up to six months. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Coffee Board of India. 

The Coffee Board operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 

Farmers can contact the Coffee Board at their regional offices for assistance. 

The board also provides resources and guidance on eco-certification processes. 

The scheme has a significant impact on the livelihood of coffee growers. 

It aims to improve the quality of coffee produced in India. 

By promoting eco-certification, the scheme helps in enhancing the sustainability of coffee farming. 

The government has allocated INR 100 crore for the implementation of this scheme over five years. 

This funding is intended to support various activities related to eco-certification. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness among farmers about the benefits of sustainable practices. 

It encourages farmers to adopt organic farming methods to improve soil health. 

The Coffee Board conducts workshops and training sessions regularly. 

These sessions cover topics such as pest management and soil conservation techniques. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of biodiversity in coffee cultivation. 

Farmers are encouraged to maintain shade trees and other vegetation in coffee plantations. 

This practice not only enhances the quality of coffee but also supports local ecosystems. 

The eco-certification process includes several standards that must be met. 

These standards are set by international bodies such as Rainforest Alliance and Fair Trade. 

Farmers must comply with these standards to obtain certification. 

The certification process involves an assessment of farming practices and environmental impact. 

Once certified, farmers can market their coffee as eco-friendly. 

This can lead to higher prices in the market due to increased consumer demand for sustainable products. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of organic fertilizers and pesticides. 

Farmers are encouraged to reduce their reliance on chemical inputs. 

This not only benefits the environment but also improves the health of consumers. 

The government has also partnered with various NGOs to support this initiative. 

These organizations assist in training and capacity building for farmers. 

They also help in the certification process by providing technical support. 

The overall goal of the scheme is to create a sustainable coffee economy in India. 

By promoting eco-certification, the government aims to position Indian coffee as a premium product globally. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance the agricultural sector in India. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme regularly. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The success of this scheme can lead to increased employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It can also contribute to the overall economic development of traditional coffee-growing regions. 

The initiative is a significant step towards promoting sustainable agriculture in India. 

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting farmers and enhancing their livelihoods. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to ensure that coffee farming remains viable and profitable for future generations.
